title: Policy-driven canary decisioning harness for deterministic progressive delivery
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: As Redwood expands LTS and mixed-channel deployments (hosted + dedicated + private), we need a deterministic, auditable canary decisioning harness that unifies feature-flag ramping, metric-based gates, and automatic rollback. Current ad-hoc ramps rely on engineers watching dashboards; this ticket builds an automated policy layer that evaluates multi-metric health fingerprints and decides progression/rollback according to guardrails.

Goals:
- Provide a policy DSL that operators and PMs can author (percent ramps, time windows, metric thresholds, region-scoped overrides).
- Integrate with our feature-flag service to drive precise percent traffic shifts per cohort.
- Compute a rollback_score from weighted metrics (latency percentiles, error rates, model degradation signals, customer error events) and perform automated rollback when thresholds crossed.
- Support dry-run & shadowing modes: mirrored traffic scoring without customer impact, and dry-run recommendations surfaced in Console.
- Emit clear audit trail (who/what/when) for each decision for compliance and postmortems.

Design notes:
- Policy DSL: YAML-like rules. Example rule: "if p95_latency > baseline * 1.4 for 5m OR api_error_rate > baseline + 0.5% for 3m => halt and rollback". Policies can be laminated (global -> org -> deployment) and bound to releases or LTS channels.
- Metrics used: p50/p95/p99 latency, 4xx/5xx rates, user-visible-error events (frontend logs), model-quality regression signal (eval-run delta), SLI drift (relative to 30d baseline).
- Rollback score: normalized metric deltas -> weighted sum -> mapped to action tiers (notice / pause / rollback). Initial weights: latency 30, error_rate 40, user_errors 20, model_quality 10. We will iterate weights after initial experiments.
- Integration points: Console rollout API, feature-flag service (server-side percentage rollouts), telemetry pipeline (time-series metrics), audit-log store, Push-to-Infra API for traffic weight changes.
- Safety nets: mandatory human-confirmation step for LTS channel promotions unless an explicit "auto-promote" flag is set for experimental customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- A policy DSL implementation accepts a rollout manifest and evaluates against live metrics to produce decisions.
- The system can programmatically advance a canary from 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% according to policy, and automatically pause/rollback when policy triggers.
- Dry-run mode exposes decisions in Console without mutating traffic.
- Audit records capture rule evaluation inputs, decision, and the triggering metric window.
- End-to-end demo with a staging rollout using a synthetic traffic generator is executed and documented.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement policy evaluator and local unit tests (this ticket).
2) Wire evaluator to Console/Backend via a decision API; add dry-run path (follow-up infra change).
3) Integrate with feature flagging service; run small shadow canaries for spike detection.
4) Run staged experiments against staging clusters, tune weights and thresholds.
5) Beta: enable for internal teams; collect feedback.
6) GA: opt-in for customers, then enable for LTS promotions with explicit guardrail enforcement.

Testing & QA:
- Synthetic traffic harness that replays production-like request distributions and error modes.
- Chaos tests (latency injection, DB errors) that validate rollback triggers.
- Regression tests for DSL parsing and evaluation edge-cases.
- Canary smoke tests: health check, synthetic end-to-end path runs post-percent-change.

Observability & dashboards:
- Rollout decisions dashboard (recent decisions, cause, scoring breakdown).
- Per-rollout metric time-series with baseline overlay.
- Alerting: when policy daemon fails to evaluate or when rollouts stuck > configured threshold.

Risks & mitigations: 
- False-positive rollbacks: mitigate with minimum window and multi-metric confirmation before destructive rollback.
- Operator confusion over policy semantics: provide a policy linter and conservative defaults.
- Security/audit: decisions must be signed and retained; security review required.
